clue.text: Wizard's local in Herts town

parts.note: Harry Potter is the boy wizard of J. K. Rowling's books, so the wizard's is Potter's
a local is the neighbourhood pub, and a bar serves the same role

explanation.surface: Somebody asks where a famous wizard drinks in a small Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is short for Hertfordshire, a county just north of London; Potters Bar is one of its towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Potters Bar is a commuter town in Hertfordshire, so it is an example of a town in that county.

clue.text: Map of factory, incomplete

indicators.note: incomplete says the word is not finished, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a plant is a factory or industrial works

explanation.surface: Someone notices that the map of the factory is unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a drawing of a site or building, close to a map.

clue.text: Appraise one in storyline, one like Brian Trubshaw?

parts.note: to appraise something is to test it

indicators.note: in puts the numeral within the word for storyline

parts.note: a plot is a storyline
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A reviewer assesses a character in a plot about a famous aviator.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Trubshaw was the British pilot who first flew Concorde in the UK; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Trubshaw flew new aircraft on trial flights, the job of an aviator who tries out new planes.

clue.text: Regular time for meeting

parts.note: regular means even, steady

explanation.surface: Someone sets a regular time for a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting such as an athletics meeting is an event, an organised occasion.

clue.text: Subordinate going on about right cocktail

indicators.note: going on means placed on top of, so in a down answer it comes first

parts.note: a side issue is a subordinate one
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A junior employee goes on about the right cocktail to mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice, an example of a mixed drink.

clue.text: Train as mobile mechanic, say

indicators.note: mobile means moving freely, so the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone trains as a mobile mechanic who drives out to fix cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mechanic' here is the old sense of a manual worker, as in Shakespeare's rude mechanicals; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker, and a mechanic in the old sense is one such craftsman.

clue.text: Report made by knight during case

indicators.note: during says one piece comes in the middle of the other, so the knight sits within the case

parts.note: a bag is a case for carrying things
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight files a report while a legal case is under way.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the loud noise of a gun firing, a synonym for an explosive sound.

clue.text: A-team notwithstanding

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: The A-team is mentioned, then brushed aside.
explanation.definitionFit: As in jokes aside, the word means setting something apart, leaving it out of account, close to notwithstanding.

clue.text: Glutton welcomes embracing start of diet — funny guy!

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so the next pieces go inside

parts.note: to welcome someone is to greet them

indicators.note: start of takes just the first letter of the word
funny suggests something odd, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A glutton welcomes the start of a diet, and what a funny guy he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' gives YGU. 'funny guy' looks like a jokey aside about the glutton, but it is the anagram signal and its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Greedy guts is a British informal term for someone who eats too much, a synonym for a glutton.

clue.text: Offer of support also set out

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: set out means laid out afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An offer of support is also laid out in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is something put forward for acceptance, a synonym for an offer such as a marriage offer.

clue.text: Article: key passage

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
a key, or cay, is a low island, and an isle is an island

explanation.surface: A grammar note: an article forms the key passage of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, a synonym for a passage.

clue.text: Decide to turn off before pit

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: to deter someone is to turn them off an idea, put them off it
a pit is a mine, as in a coal pit

explanation.surface: Someone must choose whether to switch something off before going down the pit.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine is to settle or resolve a matter, a straightforward synonym for deciding.

clue.text: Move on horseback, approaching hurdles

indicators.note: approaching puts the first piece just before the second, coming up to it

parts.note: a jockey who is up is riding, mounted on a horse
in racing slang the sticks are the hurdles or fences jumped

explanation.surface: A rider moves on horseback towards the jumps in a hurdle race.
explanation.definitionFit: To up sticks is an informal idiom for packing up and relocating, so it means to move house.

clue.text: Pressure escort to appeal

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
to escort someone is to lead them

explanation.surface: Someone pressures an escort into making an appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to make an earnest request, a synonym for appealing to someone.

clue.text: Lacking money for a buttery biscuit

parts.note: to be short of something is to be lacking it
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone short of cash has to go without a buttery biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortbread is a rich Scottish biscuit made with lots of butter, an example of a buttery biscuit.

clue.text: Put away gun, sort he loaded to protect student

indicators.note: to protect is to surround, so the second piece goes inside the first
loaded suggests the letters are packed in any old way, so they are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner plate, standing for a student

explanation.surface: A gunman is told to put his weapon away; he loaded it, so he must sort it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' rearranges SORT HE into HOSTER; 'to protect' puts L inside it. 'loaded' looks like part of the gun scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To holster a pistol is to slip it back into its leather case, the verb for putting a gun away.

clue.text: Misguided notes involving northern New York poet

indicators.note: involving means including, so the next pieces go inside
misguided means led astray, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A northern poet in New York writes wayward notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misguided' gives TESON, which is split open by the northern New York letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Lord Tennyson was a Victorian Poet Laureate, so he is an example of a poet.

clue.text: Receives inside information about savings

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the whole assembly is read backwards
inside puts the receiving word within the word for information

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information
to receive something is to get it, so receives gives gets

explanation.surface: Someone is given insider information concerning their savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside information' reads as one phrase but splits: 'inside' is the container signal, and 'about' turns the whole assembly round.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is a sum of money put aside for the future, an idiom for savings.

clue.text: Always without, failing to get by

indicators.note: failing to get says the word lacks something, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: without in its old sense means outside, externally
X is the multiplication sign, read as by, as in 3 by 4

explanation.surface: Someone who is always going without just fails to get by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense, outside. Dropping X leaves the word for always.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means for ever, without end, a synonym for always.

clue.text: Decay, reportedly beneath and round building

parts.note: to decay is to rot

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the next piece is taken by how it is said, not how it is written

parts.note: beneath means under

explanation.surface: A report says decay lies beneath a circular building.
explanation.walkthrough: UNDA is how under sounds in non-rhotic British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, often with a dome, so it is defined by its shape.

clue.text: American, leader of team leading early on

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of the word

parts.note: leading means coming first

explanation.surface: An American captain of the team took the lead early on in the game.
explanation.definitionFit: At first means at the beginning, an idiom that substitutes for early on.

clue.text: Striking foreigner in street

indicators.note: in puts the foreigner within the abbreviation for street

parts.note: an alien is a foreigner, someone from another country

explanation.surface: A foreign worker is out on strike in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' suggests industrial action but means noticeable.
explanation.definitionFit: A salient feature stands out and catches the eye, so it is a synonym for striking or prominent.

clue.text: Narrow lake in poster

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for poster

parts.note: a poster is one who posts a letter, a sender

explanation.surface: A slim lake appears in a poster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poster' is not a wall picture but one who posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means slim, thin in width, a synonym for narrow.

clue.text: Check the compiler's not all there

parts.note: to check something is to bar or block it
the setter speaking of themselves, so the compiler's means my

explanation.surface: The setter checks and admits they are not entirely sane.
explanation.walkthrough: Barmy is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not all there is slightly mad, and barmy is an informal synonym for mad.

clue.text: True masculine domain

parts.note: true means real, genuine

explanation.surface: A truly masculine domain is described.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom or sphere of activity, a synonym for domain.

clue.text: Skilfully handling English novelist

definitions.meaning: ... questions is dealing with them deftly
Henry ... was the 18th-century author of Tom Jones

explanation.surface: An English writer is praised for his deft handling of material.
explanation.definitionFit: Fielding questions means coping with them well, and Henry Fielding wrote Tom Jones.

clue.text: Showy dresser, extremely dishy?

definitions.meaning: a fop, a man who dresses to be admired
as an old-fashioned adjective it means first-rate, splendid

explanation.surface: A flamboyant dresser is thought very attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: The extremes of 'dishy' are D and Y, which spelt out in full gives the answer; the question mark flags that playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy is a man devoted to stylish clothes, and as an adjective the word means excellent or fine.

clue.text: Girl in papers supporting soldiers heading off

indicators.note: in a down answer supporting means coming underneath, so this piece is placed second
heading off removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: soldiers are men, the rank and file
ID, identity documents, are papers

explanation.surface: A girl's papers support soldiers heading off to war.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female first name, as in Enid Blyton, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Smitten with cycling star — our editor!

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: a star is a big name, a celebrity
taken as written

explanation.surface: Our editor is besotted with a celebrity who cycles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the E of NAME to the front, giving ENAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To be smitten is to be infatuated, in love, which enamoured describes.

clue.text: Synthetic material you'll find in many longbows

indicators.note: you'll find in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Bowstrings of man-made fibre are common on modern longbows.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a man-made polymer fibre, an example of a synthetic material.

clue.text: Obscure European coin worth ten cents

parts.note: to obscure is to dim, make less clear

explanation.surface: An obscure European coin is valued at ten cents.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime is the American coin worth one tenth of a dollar.

clue.text: Naively optimistic, continued drinking whiskey next to Romeo

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the drink goes inside the first word

parts.note: to have stayed is to have continued or remained

indicators.note: next to puts the two pieces side by side

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
rye is an American whiskey made from rye grain

explanation.surface: Romeo, hopelessly idealistic, kept on drinking whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: Rye is a whiskey distilled mainly from rye grain, common in America and Canada; the drink splits the verb after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being starry-eyed means having a dreamy, unrealistic outlook, an idiom for naive optimism.
